# v0.30.2: the merged-reply loss fix

v0.30.2 is a patch release on v0.30.1. It changes how LCM-X credits tool calls and tool results that sit before its resume point, which fixes the merged-reply loss, the first item under Known issues in v0.30.1. It changes no setting and no schema. The [v0.30.1 notes](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/tag/v0.30.1) still apply, except where this page says otherwise.

## Fixed

- **An assistant reply that calls tools is no longer counted as stored without being stored, on both reproduced routes of the merged-reply loss.**
  - Hermes merges two user messages in a row into one before the model call (for example, in a group chat, or when a second message arrives before the agent replies). The agent's first reply then sits before LCM-X's resume point.
  - v0.30.0 and v0.30.1 counted that reply as already stored without storing it. Its tool results were stored, and Hermes's own transcript still holds the reply. Conversation length did not matter.
  - Tests reproduce both routes: one where the lookup described below stops early, and one where every row the audit compares is accounted for, so on v0.30.1 no lookup ran ([#3019](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3019), ported to main in [#3020](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/3020)).
- **How tool rows before the resume point are credited.**
  - For unmatched tool calls and tool results in the changed part of the list before the resume point, LCM-X now looks up their call ids even when the audit found no missing row. The lookup searches the rows stored for the current session, its verified ancestors and its recorded rotation predecessors. LCM-X stores the rows it does not find, when they pass the lookup's id, ignore and tool-group checks.
  - The lookup stops early at its row, byte or id budget, on a failed read, on a stored tool call in a non-standard format, or on lineage it cannot verify. Then an eligible row keeps its credit when a row of the same kind with the same ids sat below the resume point that the session's previous completed ingest published, and LCM-X stores the other eligible rows. That earlier list records what the host sent, not what was stored.
  - Where it cannot tell, it leans toward storing: a possible second copy rather than a possible loss.
- **Three v0.30.1 known issues about moved tool rows are narrowed.** "Some moved tool rows are still skipped", "Large or non-standard tool histories keep the old loss behaviour" and "Unreadable ancestry limits moved-row recovery" ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)) describe unmatched tool rows before the resume point that stayed counted as replays and were not stored. Those rows now go through the lookup and its fallback above. Tests show a moved tool call stored past the lookup's row and byte limits, and a new tool call stored with its result after a failed presence read; the tests that pinned the #2467 loss as an expected failure now pass. The #2116 loss of a replaced unstamped reply remains, and a replaced or inserted tool pair ([#2452](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2452)) is not claimed fixed.

## Known issues

- **Replies lost before this release are not restored by it.** Hermes's own transcript still holds them. A transcript-based repair is planned for v0.30.3 ([#3022](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3022)).
- **A tool call that an earlier pass left unstored behind its stored result stays unstored.** This is the v0.30.1 item "A tool call can stay unstored when its result is already stored". On a later ingest whose lookup stops early, the previous completed ingest's list still holds that call, so it stays counted as stored, as on v0.30.1. In a related case, a fresh result whose call an earlier pass lost is now stored without that call, where v0.30.1 lost the result too; the tool-pair guard leaves that lone result out of what the model sees. The v0.30.3 repair is planned to restore such calls from Hermes's transcript ([#3022](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3022)).
- **This release can store a second copy of a tool call and its result where v0.30.1 would not.** It needs the lookup to stop early, and a call and result that LCM-X stored without their host timestamp, either on the first ingest after a restart or a session rotation, or after that call and result left the conversation and came back. Nothing is lost: recall can return them twice.
- **Nine shapes still lose or copy a tool row when the lookup stops early** ([#3023](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3023)). How often they occur is not measured. Each is no worse than v0.30.1.
  - A tool call is missing while its result is stored: the clean call that takes the place of an ignored call whose assistant text was quarantined while its tool-call ids remained, or of an ignored call whose placeholder LCM-X could not reuse because the host changed an earlier part of the turn.
  - A fresh tool result is not stored: a real result that replaces an ignored one whose placeholder digest has left the 512-entry registry; the other result of a parallel call whose id repeats on two result rows, or in which redaction rewrites only one id; a fresh result of an unstamped stored call in the prefix, after a pass that could not audit the prefix left that call out of its list, the prefix was restored and the next lookup stopped early; and a fresh result whose call sits before the audit's start and was not in the previous ingest's list.
  - A row is stored twice: an unstamped stored result that a restored call shifts to the resume point, or, in theory, a genuine tool output that reproduces a registered placeholder marker exactly, on a later shifted lookup that stops early.
- **Some rows keep v0.30.1's behaviour and can be left unstored:** a tool call or tool result whose id repeats in the list, even within a single call; a row whose id cannot be read; and a tool result whose call is not stored, not being stored and not in the previous ingest's list.

## Upgrade and rollback

- **Upgrade.** No setting changes and no schema change.
- **Rollback.** Take a SQLite-safe backup first (see `docs/operator-guide.md`). The rollback target is v0.30.1. Rows that v0.30.2 stored stay in the store as ordinary rows. After a rollback, the v0.30.1 known issues apply to that store again, the merged-reply loss included.

## Qualification

The fix changes the ingest audit, a storage path, so it ships on the careful lane, scoped to the fix's mechanism (release decision T1-482): the new tests and the targeted regression suites, without the full release campaign.
- `tests/test_merged_user_reply_loss.py` fails on v0.30.0, on v0.30.1 and on main before its port, and passes with the fix. Cells in `tests/test_topic9_loss_clause.py` and `tests/test_topic9_loss_cells_t1486.py` cover both routes of the loss. The fix's lane removed eight of its mechanisms one at a time, and each removal made a cell fail.
- CI on the fix's final commit ([run 44994888137](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/actions/runs/44994888137)) failed the same 9 of 36 jobs as v0.30.1's product commit c62f3b12 ([run 44949714507](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/actions/runs/44949714507)): lint, on two unused imports in one test file; four test shards, on one compatibility test that needs a v0.30.0 commit the release line's CI does not fetch; and the four jobs that collect those shards. Both causes are test and CI fixes tracked in [#3021](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3021). The Real Hermes host and Differential workflows passed on that commit.
- Review: two independent reviewers, one Codex and one Claude, over three rounds. Round 3 found one regression: with redaction on, a redacted tool call that Hermes echoed back was stored again when the lookup stopped early. It was fixed, a test now covers it, and both re-checks of the fix found nothing. One redaction case is proven by code reading only: a raw host id that matches a redacted active copy through the previous ingest's list.
- Not run for this release, by the same decision: the full release campaign, including the real-store and benchmark rows.
